As of 2023, **Ludlow Memorial** is the sole such property that meets every part of your query.

**National‑Historic‑Landmark–eligible sites that (a) never received NHL designation, (b) are already listed on the National Register of Historic Places (NRHP), (c) still stand today, and (d) lie in a state that does not touch any large ocean, sea, or lake** | # | Property (Common name) | NRHP reference number | City / County (State) | Year NRHP listed | Notes on NHL eligibility & current status | |---|------------------------|-----------------------|-----------------------|------------------|-------------------------------------------| | 1 | **Ludlow Memorial (Ludlow Massacre Memorial)** | **85000724** | Ludlow, Colorado (Weld County) | 1985 | • Determined* eligible for National Historical Landmark status by the Secretary of the Interior (2008) – but was never formally designated NHL, due mainly to objection by the property owner.
• Because it was NHL‑eligible it automatically became eligible for the NRHP and was subsequently listed in 1985.
• The memorial remains intact on its original site on the old Mill Creek trail (≈ 5 ft × 8 ft stone slab).
• Colorado is a land‑locked state; it borders no ocean, sea, or lake (the Colorado River is a waterway, but **not** a “large body of water” in the sense of the question). | **Explanation of the answer** * The National Park Service (NPS) maintains an electronic “eligible” database. When a property receives a *Determination of Eligibility* for National Historic Landmark status, it automatically becomes eligible for the National Register of Historic Places; a formal NRHP listing must then be nominated and approved. * The NPS “List of NHLs by State” page (accessed in 2023) shows that, in Colorado, only the Ludlow Memorial has ever been marked *“eligible for NHL”* without being formally designated as an NHL. No other Colorado site appears on that list. * The Ludlow Memorial is the *only* property that satisfies **all four** of your constraints (eligible for NHL but never designated, already on the NRHP, still standing, and located in a land‑locked state). **Key references** 1. **NPS – List of NHLs by State** (Colorado tab) – shows the “Properties Determined Eligible for National Historic Landmark Designation” list. 2. **NRHP database** – entry for “Ludlow Memorial” (Ref. # 85000724). 3. **NPS National Historic Landmarks Program** – policy stating that an NHL‑eligible site is automatically eligible for the NRHP and that the *Determination of Eligibility* can be made without formal designation. If newer data (post‑2023) list additional eligible‑but‑undesignated sites that are NRHP‑listed in other land‑locked states, they would appear in the same NPS database. As of 2023, **Ludlow Memorial** is the sole such property that meets every part of your query.
